summary: Nora can now make a document when somebody asks for one: a plan, report, comparison or itinerary that people open later in the web app, signed in, in the app's own look.
details: Ask her in a chat for a document and she writes it, checks it and publishes it. It appears under Documents in the web app, where it can be opened, archived, deleted and restored.

A document is built from a fixed set of parts: sections, prose, tables, stats, timelines, charts, diagrams, maps and pictures from the room. It cannot carry a script or a web page of its own, and a document that breaks the rules is refused with a plain list of what to fix, never half shown.

Only people the document's room names, and whoever asked for it, can open it. Anyone else gets the same "not one of your documents" page as for a document that does not exist. There is no public link.
Ask her to change a document and she edits the same one, so its link stays the same; if somebody changed it meanwhile she reads it again first instead of overwriting.
A picture goes in only if it came from the same room in the last 90 days, and she says which pictures she used.
She sees the room's most recent documents at the start of each turn, so a later "make it 8pm" finds the right one.
limitations: There is no search across documents, no slide view, no print or PDF view and no way to browse a document's earlier revisions yet.
A reply carries a link to the document only when the web app's address is configured; until then she says it is under Documents, by its title.
Forgetting a person does not yet remove the documents they made.
A picture older than 90 days cannot be used, and a document is not the way to send a file: files (a spreadsheet, a PDF) are sent as attachments or links instead.
